description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Mortimer Trap. Don't grab on e5 — develop and keep the Spanish pressure.

drills.briefExplanation: 4.d3 Ne7 5.O-O! Ng6 6.Re1 — the quiet Spanish setup; ignore the e5 pawn.
drills.description: White to play. Black plays 3...Nf6 — meet the Berlin and the coming Mortimer solidly.
drills.explanation: The correct attitude against the Mortimer: 4.d3, and after 4...Ne7 simply 5.O-O!. White refuses the poisoned 5.Nxe5? and keeps the Spanish bind — after 5...Ng6 6.Re1 the rook eyes e5, the b5 bishop still pressures c6, and Black's knight is passive on g6. The trap only snaps on greed.
drills.name: Ignoring the Bait

drills.briefExplanation: 5.Ba4! Ng6 6.O-O c6 7.Bb3 — retreat along the diagonal and keep the pressure.
drills.description: White to play. Black played the Mortimer 4...Ne7 — retreat and castle.
drills.explanation: 5.Ba4! is White's most flexible reply: the bishop steps off the c6-attack before ...c6 comes, keeping the pin on the d7 pawn (note 6...d6?? would be illegal — the pawn is pinned to the king). After 5...Ng6 6.O-O c6 White retreats 7.Bb3, keeping the Spanish pressure with Black's knight slightly misplaced — a small but lasting edge, and zero risk.
drills.name: The Ba4 Retreat
